title: Summing up: markers for an argument

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *en resumen* from B1 Unit 13, together with *lo más importante es que* and *destaca que*, the markers for building and closing an argument. They move a text from facts to a conclusion. When you judge the new democracies, they help you keep what the sources say apart from your own view.

items.spanish: En resumen, la región tenía democracias, pero muchas eran imperfectas.
items.english: In summary, the region had democracies, but many were imperfect.

items.spanish: Lo más importante es que muchos ciudadanos pedían más que elecciones.
items.english: The most important thing is that many citizens asked for more than elections.

items.spanish: El politólogo Guillermo O'Donnell destaca que los presidentes tenían pocos controles.
items.english: The political scientist Guillermo O'Donnell points out that presidents had few checks.

items.spanish: En resumen, las elecciones eran necesarias, pero no suficientes.
items.english: In summary, elections were necessary, but not enough.

sections.content: Put the marker first and a comma after it (*en resumen,*). *Lo más importante es que* is followed by a full clause. Use one closing marker, not several: a good summary says what happened and what matters most.
